claim: A: a 28.6 x 1.65 mm 6061-T6 rung carries the 1.47 kN climber load (100 kg x 1.5) at mid-span
law: Simply supported beam, M = F L / 4; hollow circular section modulus; 6061-T6 yield 240 MPa

claim: A: each foam-sleeved rung floats with at least 0.15 kg of spare lift (before the rope share)
law: Archimedes: foam displaces water, bore floods through the rope holes, aluminium wall sinks
closed_by: CNR-CAL-001 C1 (with the rope and fittings share)

claim: A: two wet 9 mm EN 1891 type B ropes with stopper knots hold four times the 4.5 kN anchor target (equal sharing; after the 20 percent ageing allowance of R8 the figure is 14.7 kN, a factor of 3.3)
law: Catalogue minimum breaking strength 18 kN x knot efficiency 0.60 x wet 0.85 (to be proof-loaded)

claim: A: the 500 x 1,200 mm footing holds 1.5 x 4.5 kN in drained granular soil
law: Broms (1964) short rigid pile, cohesionless soil, free head: Hu = 0.5 g D L^3 Kp / (e + L); g 18 kN/m3, phi 30 deg
check: 16.1 kN against 6.75 kN on level ground; the post is 1.0 m behind a 1.5:1 lined slope, so the passive wedge is cut and a slope-crest reduction applies that CNR-CAL-001 does not include (independent review, finding 1)

claim: A: the same footing holds 1.5 x 4.5 kN in saturated soil
law: Broms (1964) with submerged unit weight 8 kN/m3
check: 7.2 kN against 6.75 kN on level ground, only 7 percent over; the slope-crest reduction is not applied, so the margin may not exist (independent review, finding 1); site pull test

claim: A: a person holding on in a 2 m/s current, plus climbing, loads the anchor to less than 4.5 kN
law: Drag F = 0.5 rho Cd A v^2 (Cd A 0.35 m2) plus 1.47 kN climbing on a vertical wall

claim: A: the 4,020 mm rung section reaches the water on the 1.5:1 design slope with two rungs in it
law: Slope length to the water line from the coping, less the top offset, plus one more pitch

claim: A: one adult throws the 4.27 kg ladder (as thrown) the 3 m to the water
law: Projectile range v^2/g at 45 deg; kinetic energy 0.5 m v^2 against 300 W peak over 0.3 s (limits.HUMAN_PEAK_W)

claim: A: a nylon rope bush takes the full 1.47 kN of a foot at one rung end on a 2 mm contact band (CNR-CAL-001 uses 750 N per end)
law: Flange bearing stress, F over a 2 mm contact band (a quarter of the 22 mm flange ring), against water-saturated nylon (PA6) yield taken as 35 MPa (dry about 50 MPa; class values, datasheet to cite)
closed_by: CNR-CAL-001 D3 (750 N per end); proof load at TRL 4

claim: A: ropes, rungs and foam keep 80 percent of strength after 2 years of outdoor storage
law: Polyester and polyamide lose strength under UV; the opaque UV-stabilised box limits exposure to use and inspection
check: Consistent with the literature on UV ageing of rope; the retained strength is a test result, not a calculation

claim: A: an aluminium mounting plate clamped on a galvanised steel post does not corrode through in 2 years
law: Zinc and aluminium sit close together in the galvanic series in neutral water, so the couple is weak; the plate sits behind an HDPE box
check: No calculation; plausible, to watch at TRL 4 (RSK failure mode F8)

claim: A: a person in 5 to 30 C water can grip and climb a 335 mm rung pitch in under 60 s
law: Cold-water immersion reduces grip strength and coordination within minutes; 6 rungs at about 5 s each is 30 s for a fit adult, much more for a child or a cold person
check: A supervised tank trial is the only real check (TRL 4); no fix is possible on paper

claim: B: a 25.4 x 3.2 mm 6061-T6 rung carries a 1.5 kN climber load at mid-span (the first design used a 1.6 mm wall: 206 MPa, 0.86 of yield, a fail; fixed to 3.2 mm, same outside diameter)
law: Simply supported beam, M = F L / 4; hollow circular section; 6061-T6 yield 240 MPa
closed_by: DEC fix under the 2026-10-23 instruction; not in CNR-CAL-001

claim: B: each RHS 25 x 45 x 2 stile bridges 1.8 m between wall pads under a climber
law: Point load at mid-span, shared by two stiles, strong axis of the 45 mm depth

claim: B: the 10 mm lanyard holds the along-slope part of a climber (0.82 kN) with a factor of 4
law: A catalogue breaking strength for the 10 mm rope is not cited (to assess); if it matches the 9 mm rope of S3 (9.2 kN with knots, wet) the factor is 11
check: Unknown until a datasheet is cited; the vertical-wall case (1.6 kN) is not checked

claim: B: the splice sleeve bolts pass the stile bending moment by bearing on a 2 mm wall (the first design put the splice at mid-span: 188 MPa, a fail; fixed by moving the splice onto the wall pad)
law: Support moment of a stile continuous over the pad 3 P L / 32; couple over two M5 bolts 176 mm apart; bearing area 5 mm x 2 mm wall; 6061-T6 yield 240 MPa
closed_by: DEC fix under the 2026-10-23 instruction; not in CNR-CAL-001

claim: B: one adult carries and lowers the 10.6 kg ladder over the coping
law: Mass against the 23 kg load constant of the NIOSH lifting equation (ideal case); lowering a 4.7 m ladder at arm's length over an edge counts for much less
check: 10.6 kg is under half of the load constant, but the cantilever when lowering is a lever of about 1 m

claim: C: one adult hand-cranks a 100 kg person up the wall at 0.043 m/s (98 s for 4.2 m; handle force about 150 N)
law: Tension T = m g (sin a + mu cos a), mu 0.5 wet clothing on concrete; power T v / efficiency 0.85 against sustained human output (limits.HUMAN_SUSTAINED_W)

claim: C: the RHS 100 x 60 x 4 boom carries the sheave reaction 1.43 m from the post
law: Sheave resultant T x |sum of the two rope directions| = 1.2 T; moment on the boom root; S235

claim: C: the 600 x 1,200 mm footing resists the overturning moment of the boom
law: Broms limit moment 0.5 g D L^3 Kp at a large load height, against 1.5 x the moment at ground level (g 18 kN/m3, phi 30 deg)

claim: C: the float collar (torus of 270 mm major radius and 55 mm minor radius) displaces enough water to support a clothed adult; head-up stability is not checked
law: Torus volume 2 pi^2 R r^2 displaces water; an adult's negative buoyancy is taken as 5 kg (screening value, to be confirmed)

claim: C: the 8 mm rescue rope holds the 1.0 kN haul with a factor of 5
law: A catalogue minimum breaking strength for 8 mm low-stretch kernmantle rope is not yet cited (to assess); 8 mm is below the 9 mm that CNR-DDR-003 judged the minimum for A
check: Unknown until a datasheet is cited

claim: A: the forged M16 eye nut holds the 4.5 kN with a factor of 1.5 at the real pull angle
law: DIN 582 class working load limit 700 kg applies in line with the thread; the rope pulls the eye 14 to 34 degrees off the bolt axis down the slope and across the canal, where a rating is lower (value to cite)
check: In line the factor is 1.53; off axis it is not shown (independent review, finding 6); fix proposed to Amish (CNR-DEC-001)
